iPhone Duo will debut on October 23, but its StandBy mode has several hidden features that have not been announced yet, recently discovered in Apple code.

iPhone Duo's StandBy mode will provide a variety of unprecedented additional screens

When iPhone Duo launches next month, it will be the most versatile iPhone ever. In addition to featuring dual screens, it also offers various special modes in different usage forms.

You can fold or unfold iPhone Duo, place it vertically or horizontally, and choose between "sitting" or "standing" forms.

The standing form is ideal for watching videos, and also enables a series of brand new StandBy features. Moreover, unlike previous iPhones, you can still use StandBy mode even when iPhone Duo is not charging.

Apple demonstrated several StandBy examples at its launch event earlier this month. However, tipster pdfu has just discovered more features that have not been announced.

According to pdfu's post, the code reveals five never-before-announced new StandBy screens:

  • Home Camera
  • Home Modular
  • Flow
  • Fade
  • Snoopy

The first two allow you to view single camera feeds or a grid array of multiple camera feeds, or set up smart home control options yourself. pdfu believes Flow will display some kind of interactive art, while Fade has no details for now but may be similar. The Snoopy screen is expected to be similar to the Apple tvOS screensaver.

These new screens will sit alongside the previously revealed StandBy screens, including Analog, Digital, Classic Calendar, Weather, Photos, Memories, Shared Albums, and Modular.

pdfu's full post on X also reveals how the customisation interface for multiple StandBy screens on iPhone Duo will work.

Do you expect to use StandBy mode frequently on iPhone Duo? Feel free to let us know in the comments below.
